title: Micro playbook: prefetchahead KV, route-level batching, and adaptive quant profiles
creator: Priya Menon
description:
Purpose: Create a compact, repeatable product playbook (’micro playbook’) that enables product and infra teams to safely capture first-order unit-economy savings from three levers: KV prefetch / prefix caching heuristics, route-aware batching policies, and adaptive quantization profiles.

Scope: This is a product-led guidance pack plus instrumentation and a 2-wave rollout plan targeted at 2 pilot customers and ~5 internal product routes. The deliverable includes: (a) decision flows for when to apply each lever, (b) gating SLOs and safety nets, (c) sample config templates for console + API, (d) telemetry dashboard and alert set, and (e) a short training doc for SEs and solutions.

Why now: Early Dedicated and Private customers show 12–18% token-cost variance across routes. Engineering improvements alone won’t scale without product guardrails and standardized rollout templates that prevent quality regressions. This playbook aims to reduce token-level cost by 8–15% on targeted routes while keeping p99 latency and quality regressions within agreed thresholds.

acceptance_criteria: 1) Playbook doc with decision flow and sample configs published in Confluence and linked from Console help

2) Telemetry: per-route baseline and live comparison panels showing token-cost, cost-per-request, p50/p95/p99 latency, and a quality regression metric (BLEU/ROUGE or model-specific eval) for pilot routes
3) Pilot applied to 2 customer routes and 3 internal routes without quality regression >2% on eval set and p99 latency increase <15%
4) Rollback & safety nets: automatic fallback policy configured if quality or latency thresholds breached, and rollback exercised in a canary test
5) Console: route-level toggles for batching window, KV prefetch boolean + TTL, and quant profile selector with preview of estimated cost impact
